name: Zero-Incline Chest-Supported Row
description: The zero-incline (fully flat/horizontal) chest-supported row places the bench at zero degrees, requiring the lifter to row the dumbbells from a fully horizontal prone position. With the torso fully parallel to the floor, the row produces a more vertical pull than inclined versions, heavily recruiting the lower lats and teres major and minimizing upper trap contribution — an ideal configuration for lower lat development.

execution.starting_position: Elevate a flat bench on two sturdy platforms (boxes, plates, or steps) so that the arms can hang below bench level when lying flat. Lie prone on the bench. Hold a dumbbell in each hand hanging beneath the bench.
execution.setup_instructions: The bench must be elevated enough that full arm extension allows the dumbbells to hang below bench height. Usually 30-50 cm elevation is sufficient depending on arm length and dumbbell size.
steps: Step 1: Begin lying flat, arms hanging down with dumbbells below bench level.
Step 2: Row both dumbbells toward the hips simultaneously, driving elbows back.
Step 4: Lower under full control back to full arm extension.
Step 5: Maintain flat body position throughout — no hip extension or arch.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Bench not elevated enough — the dumbbells must clear the floor at full extension
Elbows flaring wide — keep them moderately tucked for lower lat emphasis
safety_considerations: Ensure the elevated bench setup is stable before loading
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension (dumbbells below bench) to elbows behind torso.
coaching_cues: Row to the hips, not the chest
Feel the lower lat at the bottom stretch
